title: simone-aml-tinkerpad-2026-03-21
content:
Quick morning scratchpad - capturing fragments before they evaporate. Use this as source-of-truth for small experiments, then formalize a runbook if anything sticks.

Context
- purpose: fast, low-friction microbench and prompt comp for LLM-inference tradeoffs (quality vs cost/latency).
- model family: Llama-2 13B (baseline), trying 4-bit GS quant and 8-bit NF4, test fallback behaviors on smaller GPU instance.
- infra: dedicated dev box (A100-80GB sandbox), local serving binary from pr 789.

Recent runs (lab log)
1) run id: simone-q-r1 (2026-03-20 10:15)
   - config: Llama-2-13B, 4-bit GS, blocksize 128, kv-cache enabled, batchsize 1, int8-fallback off
   - commands: ./serve --model l2-13b --quant gs4 --block 128 --kv-cache on --port 8080
   - observations: cold-start latency ~ 320ms per first token, steady-state token latency ~ 38ms. CPU memory modest. Model load time 62s (could optimize).
   - qualitative: short completion style prompts look OK, occasional tokenization oddities in numeric tables.

2) run id: simone-q-r2 (2026-03-20 13:05)
   - config: same as r1 but batchsize 2, prefix-caching enabled for repeated prompts
   - observations: amortized token latency ~ 45ms (higher than expected likely due to micro-batching overhead), throughput improved ~1.7x for multi-turn eval sets.
   - anomaly: under heavy micro-batching, kv cache hits seem not applied for turn 2 sometimes; need to reproduce with trace.

3) run id: simone-q-r3 (2026-03-20 16:40)
   - config: 8-bit NF4 quant, batchsize 1, blocksize 256, kv-cache on
   - observations: steady token latency ~ 28ms, quality regression small on rare math prompts (precision loss). Lower memory footprint; model load 44s.

Quick numbers summary
- baseline (fp16) token latency single = ~22ms
- nf4 token latency single = ~28ms, occasional quality delta on numeric tasks
- gs4 token latency single = ~38ms, quality closer to baseline than nf4 on conversational prompts but slower than nf4
- load times: fp16 34s, nf4 44s, gs4 62s

Prompt sets used (short list)
- pmt-1: persona-chat-short (10 dialogues) - checks coherence across turns
- pmt-2: math-precision (20 Qs) - arithmetic + unit conversions
- pmt-3: table-fill (10 prompts) - expects structured numeric outputs
- pmt-4: code-synthesis small (5 examples) - python one-liners

Notes on prompts: prefer shorter system instruction, avoid long temperature sweeps in these microbench runs. For eval consistency pin max_tokens and sampling seed.

Open hypotheses / things to check
- H1: GS4 implementation's kernel selection is choosing non-optimal CUDA paths causing load/time penalty. Recompile with nvcc flags from pr 742 and re-run.
- H2: KV cache miss pattern in r2 caused by cache key normalization difference when using prefix-caching; instrument trace to dump cache keys on miss.
- H3: NF4 faster steady-state because kernels use fused attention variant; quality drop due to quant error on small integers. Try per-layer outlier scaling on embed layer.

Immediate TODOs (prioritized)
- [ ] reproduce kv-cache miss with deterministic reproduce script (target: today) -> create ticket AI-4572 (linked). Owner: Simone.
- [ ] run kernel-bench with nvcc flags -O3 and measure load times (Devon assigned).
- [ ] sweep blocksize 64/128/256 with gs4 to see latency vs memory tradeoff (Naomi).
- [ ] add seed=42 to all eval scripts and lock vocab tokenization version to v2.1
- [ ] snap logs and upload to artifact store, label with simone-q-r* ids.

Small experimental checklist / reproducible commands
- eval script: python tools/run_eval.py --model l2-13b --quant gs4 --batch 1 --block 128 --prompt-file prompts/pmt-1.json --seed 42 --out results/simone-q-r1.json
- kernel bench: tools/kernel_bench --model l2-13b --quant gs4 --nvcc-args "-O3 -arch=sm_80" --run-id simone-kb-1
- kv trace helper: python tools/kv_trace.py --serve-port 8080 --trace-out traces/simone-kv-r2.log

Quick scratch markdown of possible note to formalize later:
- Add a short micro-runbook: when testing quant, always: (1) lock tokenizer, (2) pin seed, (3) snapshot model bytes, (4) record load+steady lat separately.

Misc mental notes
- remember: prioritize reproducible triage over chasing tiny latency wins. If nvcc flags reduce load by 20s, that's higher uplift than micro 2ms token latency.
- ask runtime team about pre-warming options on Dedicated to hide load time for cold starts.

Links and refs
- PR with local serving changes: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/789
- KV cache design notes: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/AM/kv-cache-notes
- Related ticket: JIRA AI-4572 (kv-cache miss repro)

End of scratchpad. Will tidy and move high-confidence items to a runbook doc if we get a clean repro.
